name: Fertiliser supply
value: Egypt urea $500/t FOB; Hormuz still impeded
summary: Egyptian urea sold at $500 a tonne in the week to 20 Nov as prices steady; Hormuz urea transits highest since June
state: IFDC said on 24 Nov that urea prices have been broadly stable since a correction in October, with granular urea sold at $500 a tonne FOB Egypt in the week to 20 Nov, below the $535 quoted early in November (EnterpriseAM). Nine urea-laden vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz in November, the most since June, and Egyptian producers cut output by 20–33% after gas supply cuts (IFDC). Gulf exports still rely on an impeded Hormuz route, so Watch holds; no export bans by several major exporters were found.
for_you: Farmers face higher fertiliser costs than before the Gulf war, which can feed into food prices over later seasons. Prices could move sharply either way depending on events in the Gulf.
rubric_hit: Watch: urea rise below +30% in 3 months, but Gulf exports rely on an impeded Hormuz route; no multi-exporter bans

sources.title: EnterpriseAM — Egyptian granular urea at USD 535 as gas supplies to fertilizer plants cut 20%

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
